scope: Read-only review of stable semantic coverage and test-contract gaps. This is not acceptance and does not assess temporary syntax while the owner is editing.

notes: The seven canonical state values match D4 exactly.

Existing tests cover direct object maps, matching and mismatched tokens, literals, CSS selectors, direct JSX conditions, switch cases, spreads, computed keys, parse errors, SVG attributes, and one non-exempt graph path.

findings.finding: Two property names that happen to be D4 words make an unrelated object a status map, even when neither the binding nor its context denotes status.
findings.impact: Ordinary navigation, workflow copy, visualization, or domain data with keys such as next and done can receive status-mismatch findings. This is a semantic false positive and can pressure callers to add improper exceptions.
findings.required: Require a status-bearing binding, discriminant, selector, component property, or another explicit status context before treating a multi-key object as D4 chrome. Add negative fixtures using unrelated next/done objects and positive fixtures proving a real status map still reports.

findings.finding: Shorthand properties bypass status-map value classification.
findings.impact: A copied or wrong literal can be assigned through a local alias and then inserted into STATUS_COLORS without a finding.
findings.reproducer: const done = '#EF4444'; export const STATUS_COLORS = { done }
findings.required: Resolve statically bound shorthand properties and aliases, or report status-unsupported when their value cannot be proven. Add matching-literal, mismatched-literal, matching-token, and unresolved/imported alias fixtures.

findings.finding: JSX status chrome silently accepts identifier-based style and className objects because classification handles inline literals but neither resolves nor rejects the alias.
findings.impact: The common pattern of defining a style object or class constant outside JSX bypasses D4 correlation even though the JSX exposes a literal status.
findings.reproducer: const doneStyle = { backgroundColor: '#EF4444' }; export const X = () => <div status="done" style={doneStyle} />
findings.required: Resolve local const aliases for style and className values. Emit status-unsupported for imported, mutable, parameter, or otherwise unresolved aliases. Cover nested aliases and lexical shadowing so resolution does not bind to a same-named declaration in another scope.

findings.finding: CSS status correlation covers only a narrow property-name allowlist and misses D4-governed border and state treatments.
findings.impact: D4 explicitly governs borders and hover/focus treatments, but status selectors can use a second palette through side-specific borders, text decoration, caret, shadows, or other color-bearing properties without a status finding.
findings.required: Use parsed CSS property semantics or a complete reviewed color-bearing property set instead of the current partial regular expression. Add fixtures for border side colors, outline, box-shadow, text-decoration-color, caret-color, gradients, hover/focus selectors, and custom-property indirection. Unknown dynamic color-bearing status declarations must report unsupported rather than pass.

findings.finding: The scanner accepts resolved token IDs that are absent from policy.tokenCssNames.
findings.impact: A caller can place an arbitrary entry in resolvedTokens and make an unregistered CSS variable look constitutional, bypassing the generated-token registry boundary.
findings.required: Require every accepted CSS token reference to exist in tokenCssNames as well as resolve to the correct value. Treat absent or inconsistent registry entries as status-unsupported. Add negative fixtures for an unregistered matching-value token and a registered token missing a resolved value.

findings.finding: A valid SVG style element is fed through the TSX parser and becomes a status parse error instead of being analyzed as CSS.
findings.impact: Legitimate SVGs with embedded style sheets are blocked regardless of whether their D4 paint is correct, while the declarations themselves never receive status correlation.
findings.required: Parse SVG style element contents through the CSS status path, preserving the enclosing file path and fail-closed behavior. Add matching-token, wrong-color, matching-literal, malformed-style, and CSS-variable fixtures.

findings.finding: The aliases draft→inbox, approved→next, planning→next, and running→in-progress are asserted as D4 facts, but the cited D4 definition does not declare those equivalences.
findings.impact: Plan or release lifecycle states can be forced into task semantics without a ratified equivalence, creating both false positives and an undocumented second semantic contract.
findings.required: Either cite a ratified product-state mapping that declares each equivalence and add it to the review basis, or remove the aliases from the scanner and tests. Do not infer semantic equivalence from a coincidentally similar lifecycle word.

findings.finding: Centralized-exception behavior is stated in the shared contract but is only indirectly tested by one production-like graph path.
findings.impact: A future scanner-local skip for tests, stories, generated files, visualization paths, or fake policy exception fields could pass the current suite.
findings.required: Add path-invariance fixtures that run the same D4 violation in feature, UI, graph, story, test, and generated-looking paths, and pass fake policy exclusion fields. Every scan must return the same raw finding; exact reviewed boundaries and exceptions remain solely the audit orchestrator's responsibility.

fixtures: Imported or mutable aliases report unsupported
Object.assign and Object.fromEntries status maps report unsupported when not statically provable
JSX spreads carrying status or paint report unsupported
SVG presentation attributes and inline style retain existing coverage
Malformed or dynamically unprovable status paint fails closed

disposition: Not accepted. Preserve the exact seven-state D4 map, narrow semantic context to prevent unrelated-word false positives, and close alias/style/CSS/SVG/token-registry bypasses before activation.
